title: Rollout shadow-mode: alert emulation + cost-delta preview
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Design a console surface that lets product teams run a rollout in "shadow" or "emulation" mode where new alert rules and SLO changes are evaluated against live traffic without firing real notifications. The surface must show a concise cost-delta preview, top contributing requests, and a safe rollback recommendation if the shadowed alert produces high false positives or cost spikes.

Goals:
- Reduce risk of misconfigured alerts during rollouts by letting teams dry-run alert logic.
- Make cost implications of new alert/SLO configurations visible before enabling them.
- Provide clear next steps for engineers and on-call leads when the emulation run indicates problems.

Scope of this ticket:
- Console UI for creating a rollout step with `Shadow alert` toggle and emulation timeframe selector.
- Emulation results pane: pass/fail summary, false-positive estimation, top-5 alerting rules triggered, and cost-delta preview (tokens, GPU-minutes, and estimated $).
- Lightweight timeline card that surfaces the emulation run in the incident timeline (non-incident): includes a one-click link to create a follow-up ticket or rollback.
- Prototype flows for mobile/responsive compact cards for on-call handoff context.

Out of scope (to be considered in follow-ups): automated remediation actions, billing-level chargeback integration, and long-term storage of emulation logs beyond 30 days.
acceptance_criteria: A1: User can enable 'Shadow alert' in a rollout step and pick a start/end window or 'continuous shadow' mode
A2: After emulation completes, console displays a pass/fail summary with numeric false-positive estimate and sample triggering requests
A3: Cost-delta preview shows an itemized estimate: token delta, GPU-minutes delta, and an approximate $/hour impact
A4: Users can export emulation results as a short report (CSV) and create a follow-up Linear ticket with prefilled context
A5: Timeline card is non-notifying (no paging) and includes 'Create rollback' and 'Promote to live' quick actions
A6: Prototype validated with two on-call respondents in moderated usability test with positive completion rate >= 80%
comments: 2025-01-30 - Aisha Patel: Initial sketch uploaded to Figma. Focused on compact summary + expandable detail pane. Needs engineering constraints from runtime team on what metrics are cheaply available in 1 minute windows.

2025-02-03 - Marco Li: Eng review - backend can surface per-rule trigger counts and KV-cache hit ratios for the emulation window. Cost delta will require a best-effort estimate from billing microservice; we'll add caveat copy if estimate is approximate.

2025-02-05 - UX Research (Lina Gomez): Scheduling two moderated sessions with SRE and PM participants. Goal: observe comprehension of 'shadow' semantics and whether cost preview changes configuration choices.
2025-02-08 - Design critique: Consider adding small 'confidence' badges to false-positive estimates (low/medium/high) and a short explanation tooltip on the estimation model.

2025-02-10 - Marco Li: Prototype feasibility - timeline card can be implemented as a lightweight event type. We'll need an API contract for 'emulation-run' containing sample hits and estimated_cost. Posting ENG-4011 as dependency.
2025-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Updated Figma with variant that shows 'promote' vs 'promote + notify' as separate flows. Requesting accessibility pass and microcopy review before handing off to front-end.
Follow-ups: create PM ticket for rollout policy defaults; schedule engineering spike to prototype cost estimation accuracy in production traffic)
notes_for_engineering: 1) Emulation must not trigger external notifiers (PagerDuty, Slack). Implement a 'no-op' delivery path for shadow runs.
2) Cost estimates can be coarse — surface a confidence tier and prefer conservative rounding up to avoid surprises.
3) Provide sampling of up to 25 example requests that would have triggered alerts, with headers redacted for PII.
4) Include an 'explainability' link that surfaces the rule logic and matched conditions for each sample
